echo_one.keywords: echo one delay echo slapback ping-pong tempo sync dotted eighth quarter repeats dub one knob
slider_desc: Delay amount in one move: 0 to 24 is a soft 1/16 slapback, 25 to 49 a 1/8 echo, 50 to 74 a dotted 1/8 and 75 to 100 a 1/4 note; feedback rises from 12% to 62%, the wet level to 50%, the ping-pong spread from 25 up, and the repeats get darker (low-pass 7 to 3 kHz). The time glides to each new value
uses: Slapback on vocals and guitars
Tempo echoes on leads and synths
Ping-pong throws on the end of a phrase
Dub-style long repeats
Quick delay sketches with one control
echo_one.properties: Input → tempo-locked delay per channel (host tempo, 120 bpm without one; the time glides over 80 ms; up to 2 s) → low-pass and 150 Hz high-pass in the loop → feedback, crossing sides by the ping-pong amount → mixed with dry → Output. Zero latency.

warmer.keywords: warmer warmth warm tape tube saturation analog low mids soft top mix bus master one knob
slider_desc: Warmth in one move: 0 leaves the signal untouched; higher values drive the lows and low mids (below 600 Hz) into a gentle, slightly asymmetric tape/tube curve (drive x1 to x3, even harmonics) and lift them up to +2.3 dB, ease the top down by up to 2 dB and close a soft low-pass from 20 to 9 kHz, with a small trim so the level stays close to the input
uses: Warm up a thin vocal or acoustic guitar
Round off a DI bass
Analog glue on the drum bus
A soft glow on the master
Take the edge off bright synths
warmer.properties: Input → split at 600 Hz (one pole) → lows: asymmetric tanh curve, DC removed, mixed in by Amount, +0 to +2.3 dB; highs: 0 to -2 dB → one-pole low-pass 20 to 9 kHz faded in by Amount → trim → Output. Zero latency.

closer.keywords: closer vocal voice presence proximity upfront forward compression dialogue podcast radio one knob
slider_desc: How far forward the voice comes: 0 is untouched; higher values raise the compressor's ratio (threshold -24 dBFS, up to 3:1, 5 ms attack, 120 ms release) and its make-up (up to +3 dB), a presence lift around 3.5 kHz (up to +5 dB) that eases off by up to half while the compressor works hard, and a proximity lift below 180 Hz (up to +2.5 dB)
uses: Bring a vocal to the front of a mix
Podcast and dialogue clarity
Voice-over that sits close
Lift backing vocals or a choir
Acoustic guitar that needs to speak
closer.properties: Input → peak envelope of both channels (5 ms / 120 ms) → gain computer (-24 dBFS, 1:1 to 3:1) and make-up → + band-pass at 3.5 kHz (Q 0.9) scaled by the presence amount, reduced while the gain reduction reaches 6 dB → + one-pole low-pass at 180 Hz scaled by the proximity amount → Output. Zero latency.

smoother.keywords: smoother smooth harsh harshness resonance dynamic eq soothe tame upper mids cymbals vocals one knob
slider_desc: How much harshness to soften: 0 is off; higher values lower the threshold (-14 to -20 dB of a band's share of the whole signal) and deepen the cuts (up to 10 dB) of four bands at 2, 3.15, 5 and 8 kHz. A band is cut only while it pokes out of the mix, by what it rises over the threshold
uses: Tame a harsh vocal without dulling it
Soften cymbals and hi-hats
Take the fizz off distorted guitars
Polish a bright mix bus or master
De-harsh a podcast voice
smoother.properties: Input → mono sum → power envelope (2 ms / 80 ms) → four band-pass detectors (2, 3.15, 5, 8 kHz, Q 2) with their own envelopes → each band's share of the whole signal in dB → cut = (share - threshold) × Amount, up to 10 dB → the four bands taken out of each channel one after another (x - band × (1 - gain)) → Output. Zero latency.

phase_distortion.keywords: phase distortion pd modulation delay fm self sidechain keyed bright digital grit sound design bass lead
slider_desc: How far the delay moves, up to 3 ms (on a square curve, so the low half stays subtle)
Low-pass on the signal that moves the delay: lower values make a smoother, darker bend, higher values a brighter, more ragged one
Offset added to the moving signal: the bend becomes asymmetric (even harmonics)
Turns the right channel's movement the other way, for width
What moves the delay: the track itself (Self) or the sidechain on channels 3/4
Blend with the dry signal, which is delayed by the same centre time so the blend does not comb
Output level
uses: Bright, clean grit on bass and leads
Asymmetric harmonics without clipping
Cross-modulation: one track bends another through the sidechain
Wide, shimmering texture on guitars and pads
Sound design: metallic and digital tones
phase_distortion.properties: Input → stereo delay line (8 ms) → read with linear interpolation at 1 + depth × (1 + clamp(low-passed source + bias, -1, 1)) samples, the right source scaled by 1 - 2 × spread → mixed with the dry signal read at the centre time 1 + depth → Output gain. The source is the track or the sidechain (pins 3/4). No clipping stage; latency up to 3 ms of centre delay, not reported.

lofi_comp.keywords: lofi lo-fi compressor pumping squash sample rate reduction bitcrusher wow drift beats vintage sampler hip hop drums
slider_desc: How hard it pumps: threshold from -10 to -40 dBFS and ratio from 2:1 to 20:1 together, with its own make-up gain
How fast the compressor lets go: short values pump with the beat, long values hold the sound down
Sample rate of the old sampler (low-pass and sample-and-hold); at or above the project rate it is off
Bit depth of the quantiser: lower values add grain and noise
Slow pitch drift from two slow LFOs moving a short delay (up to 4 ms)
Blend with the dry signal
Output level
uses: Lo-fi hip hop drums in one effect
Pumping, squashed drum busses
Dusty sampler sound on keys and loops
Wobbly, tape-like pitch drift
Parallel crunch with the Mix slider
lofi_comp.properties: Input → stereo-linked peak compressor (1 ms attack, Release, threshold and ratio from Squash, make-up) → short stereo delay read with linear interpolation, moved by two LFOs (0.6 and 0.17 Hz) for wow → one-pole low-pass at 0.45 × Sample Rate and sample-and-hold at Sample Rate (off at or above the project rate) → quantise to Bits → mix with the dry signal → Output gain. No latency reported.

spectral_blur.keywords: spectral blur smear shift frequency shifter tilt spectral gate fft texture ambient sound design pad drone
slider_desc: How long each frequency lingers: rising bins follow within up to 150 ms, fading bins hang on for up to 3 s, so a soft spectral tail grows out of the sound
Moves every frequency up or down by the same number of Hz: an inharmonic, metallic frequency shift
Leans the spectrum around 1 kHz, in dB per octave (flat below 100 Hz and above 10 kHz): negative is darker, positive brighter
Pushes down every frequency bin quieter than this level (a 1:3 expander per bin); at -90 it is off
Blend with the dry signal, which is delayed to match
Output level
uses: Soft spectral tails and washes on vocals, guitars and keys
Pads and drones from any sound
Metallic, robotic or bell-like tones with Shift
Spectral gating: only the strongest partials survive
Sound design and transitions
spectral_blur.properties: Input → 2048-point FFT, Hann windows, 4x overlap → each bin shifted by Shift (rounded to the bin spacing, phase kept coherent) and tilted around 1 kHz (flat below 100 Hz and above 10 kHz) → magnitude smoothed over time (Smear: up to 150 ms rising, 3 s falling; fading bins keep turning with a little Park-Miller random drift) → per-bin 1:3 expander below Gate → inverse FFT and overlap-add → mix with the delayed dry signal → Output gain. Latency 2047 samples, reported to the host.
